title: Extended localization Cech complex computes derived ideal-power torsion
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $r\geq0$ and $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in R$, put $K=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$, and let $M$ be any $R$-module, not necessarily finitely generated. Let $\Gamma_K$ be the ideal-power torsion functor [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor], so $\Gamma_K(M)=\{m:K^nm=0\text{ for some }n\geq1\}$, and set $H_K^q(M)=R^q\Gamma_K(M)$ for $q\geq0$.

For $t\in R$, write $M_t$ for localization at the powers of $t$: its fractions $m/t^a$ satisfy $m/t^a=m'/t^b$ exactly when $t^c(t^b m-t^a m')=0$ for some $c\geq0$. Define the extended alternating cochain complex $C_R(t_1,\ldots,t_r;M)$ by
$$C^0=M,\qquad C^p=\prod_{1\leq i_1<\cdots<i_p\leq r}M_{t_{i_1}\cdots t_{i_p}}\quad(1\leq p\leq r),$$
and $C^p=0$ outside $0\leq p\leq r$. The degree-zero differential sends $m$ to $(m/1)_i$. For $p\geq1$, the component of $d^p(x)$ indexed by $i_1<\cdots<i_{p+1}$ is $\sum_{a=1}^{p+1}(-1)^{a-1}x_{i_1\ldots\widehat{i_a}\ldots i_{p+1}}$, with each summand mapped to the indicated localization. These are cochain differentials. If $r=0$ the complex is $M$ in degree zero only. For every $q\geq0$ there is a natural $R$-linear isomorphism
$$H_K^q(M)\cong H^q(C_R(t_1,\ldots,t_r;M)),$$
where $H^q(C)=\ker(d^q)/\operatorname{im}(d^{q-1})$, with the incoming image zero in degree zero.
